name: Barbados
description: Barbados offers expats an idyllic Caribbean lifestyle with year-round warm weather, stunning natural beauty, and a stable, safe environment. It's a welcoming destination for those seeking a blend of relaxation, cultural richness, and modern amenities, making it suitable for retirees, remote workers, and entrepreneurs alike.
longdescription: Life in Barbados for expats is characterized by a relaxed 'island time' pace, a welcoming community, and a high quality of life. The culture is a rich blend of British heritage and vibrant Bajan traditions, evident in its institutions, cricket fandom, and festivals like Crop Over. English is the official language, making integration relatively smooth, though the local Bajan dialect is widely spoken and adds to the island's unique charm. The society values politeness, respect, family, and community, and expats who engage with local customs will find integration very achievable. The economy is service-driven, heavily reliant on tourism, international business, and a growing remote-work community. While the domestic market is small, Barbados positions itself as a professional hub with stable governance and a modern feel. Healthcare is accessible with both public and private options, though for complex procedures, expats might consider seeking treatment overseas. The cost of living is generally considered high, especially for imported goods and housing near the coasts, but can be moderated by sourcing local produce. Overall, Barbados provides a comfortable and secure environment with a focus on dignity, education, and community responsibility, making it an attractive long-term destination.

visas.name: Barbados Welcome Stamp
visas.description: The Barbados Welcome Stamp is a special 12-month visa program for non-nationals, including remote workers, freelancers, and online business owners, to live and work remotely from Barbados. Applicants must be employed by a company or own a business registered outside Barbados and are not permitted to seek local employment or provide services to local companies.
benefits: Ability to live and work remotely in Barbados for up to 12 months.
Exemption from Barbados income tax on foreign earnings.
Freedom to travel in and out of Barbados during the visa's validity.
Option to include family members (spouses and dependents) in the application.
Access to modern infrastructure, including reliable high-speed internet and quality health services.
visas.path_to_residency_description: There is a pathway to permanent residency under Section 5(2) of the Immigration Act, Cap. 190. After residing in Barbados for at least five consecutive years on a valid visa, applicants may be eligible to apply for permanent residency.
required_documents: Valid passport (scan of bio-data page for applicant and any family members over 18).
Passport-sized photographs (for applicant and any family members over 18).
Birth certificate (for applicant and any spouse/children).
Proof of relationship for dependents (e.g., marriage or birth certificates).
Income declaration certifying expected annual income of at least USD $50,000.
Proof of valid health insurance covering the entire period of stay in Barbados.

visas.name: Barbados Retirement Visa
visas.description: The Barbados Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) for Retired Property Owners allows eligible non-nationals who own property in Barbados to reside on the island for extended or indefinite periods. It is specifically designed for retirees demonstrating financial self-sufficiency and property ownership, providing a pathway to long-term residency in Barbados.
benefits: Long-term or indefinite residency in Barbados (indefinite for those over 60)
Ability to enter and depart Barbados freely
Path to permanent residency and eventually citizenship
No limitations on length of stay for eligible permit holders
Enjoy Barbados' high quality of life in a stable environment
visas.path_to_residency_description: The SERP grants long-term residency, which can be indefinite for retired property owners aged 60 and over. After five years of continuous legal residency in Barbados, individuals become eligible to apply for Barbadian citizenship.
required_documents: Completed Extension of Stay form (Form B)
Police Certificate of Character from any country resided in for 6 months or more after age 16
Title Deeds or Land Tax document as proof of property ownership in Barbados (property valued at US$300,000 or more)
Proof of financial resources to support self and dependents (e.g., bank statements, pension documents)
Certified copy of the bio-data page of the passport
Proof of relationship to dependents (if applicable)

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- Barbados Welcome Stamp: 12-month remote work visa available online
- Retirement visa available for those with passive income
- Citizens of CARICOM countries have freedom of movement

Citizenship by Descent.desc: A child born abroad to at least one Barbadian parent is eligible for citizenship by descent. If either parent was born in Barbados and is a citizen by birth, the child is deemed a citizen at birth. The child must be registered with the nearest Barbadian diplomatic representative. Requirements include the applicant's original birth certificate (and photocopy), and the original birth certificate (and photocopy) of the Barbadian parent(s). Importantly, Section 5 of the Constitution of Barbados expressly forbids cascading citizenship by descent beyond the immediate child of a Barbadian who was born in Barbados, meaning grandchildren or great-grandchildren are generally not eligible for citizenship by descent.

Naturalization.desc: Persons may acquire Barbadian citizenship by naturalization after a period of lawful residence. The requirements typically include having resided in Barbados for a minimum of five years, including the last 12 months immediately preceding the application, and for an aggregate of at least five out of the seven years prior to the 12-month period. Applicants must be of good character and intend to continue residing in Barbados. Upon approval, applicants must take an Oath of Allegiance. Evidence typically includes residence history, employment or lawful income, address continuity, tax compliance, and community ties.

Birthright.desc: A child born in the territory of Barbados generally acquires citizenship at birth, regardless of the nationality of the parents, under the principle of *jus soli*. This applies to individuals born in Barbados after November 29, 1966, with limited exceptions (e.g., children of foreign diplomats).

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreign woman who has married a citizen of Barbados may apply for citizenship through registration. This typically requires a defined period of genuine, subsisting marriage and residence. Applications require proof of cohabitation, shared address, and, if applicable, children or financial interdependence. Marriage strengthens eligibility but is not an automatic grant; character and integration conditions still apply. Required documents include the applicant's birth certificate, spouse's birth certificate and proof of citizenship, marriage certificate, and police certificates of character from countries where the applicant has resided for six months or more after the age of sixteen.

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** For the 2025 income year, individuals are taxed progressively: 12.5% on the first BBD $50,000 of taxable income, and 28.5% on income above BBD $50,000. As of income year 2026, these rates are set to decrease to 11.5% on taxable income up to $50,000 and 27.5% on income above $50,000. Residents and domiciled individuals are taxed on worldwide income, while residents not domiciled are taxed on Barbados-sourced income and foreign income remitted to Barbados. Non-residents are taxed only on income earned in Barbados.
*   **Personal Allowances:** A basic personal allowance of BBD $25,000 is available. For pensioners aged 60 or over receiving a pension, the personal allowance will increase from BBD $50,000 to BBD $75,000, effective income year 2025.
*   **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):** Effective January 1, 2024, the general corporate tax rate is 9%. Companies whose gross income is BBD $2 million or below and are registered as a Small Business are subject to a 5.5% corporate tax rate. Certain multinational enterprise (MNE) groups with annual consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more may be subject to a Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (QDMTT) of 15% from January 1, 2024.
*   **Value-Added Tax (VAT):** The standard VAT rate is 17.5% on most goods and services. Tourism and accommodation are taxed at 10%, while many basic goods are zero-rated or exempt.
*   **Other Taxes:**
    *   **Land Tax (annual):** Based on the improved value of the property, with rates ranging from exempt for the first BBD $150,000 to 1% for values over BBD $850,000 (capped at BBD $100,000).
    *   **Land Transfer Tax:** 2.5% (usually paid by the seller).
    *   **Rental Income:** 15% flat rate on net income.
    *   **No Capital Gains Tax, Wealth Tax, Inheritance Tax, or Gift Tax.**
    *   **National Insurance Scheme (NIS):** Employees contribute 11%, and employers contribute 12.75%, up to maximum insurable earnings.
    *   **Foreign Exchange Fee:** 2% on sales of foreign currency.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Barbados has a high cost of living, especially for housing (expect $1,500-$3,500 USD per month for a modern apartment/villa in popular areas) and imported groceries. Utilities, particularly electricity, are also expensive. The average monthly cost of living for a single person is around $1330 USD (without rent being $734 USD), while for a family of four, it's about $3071 USD (without rent being $2155 USD).
*   **Language:** The official language is English. While British English is taught and used in formal settings, Bajan dialect (an English-based creole with West African influences) is commonly spoken in informal settings. Most Bajans will switch to standard English if you struggle to understand their dialect.
*   **Safety:** Barbados is generally considered a very safe destination with a low crime rate, particularly in tourist and residential areas. However, petty theft, bag snatching, and vehicle break-ins can occur in crowded areas, beaches, and nightlife districts. Take normal precautions, like not leaving valuables unattended and avoiding unlit areas at night.
*   **Registration:** If staying long-term, consider registering with your embassy or consulate for alerts and assistance. For those working remotely, the Barbados Welcome Stamp program allows remote workers to reside and operate from the island for up to 12 months.
*   **Healthcare:** Barbados offers a mix of public and private healthcare. While routine and urgent care are accessible, comprehensive health insurance, including medical evacuation, is advisable for expats. For complex procedures, some may seek treatment overseas.
*   **Transportation:** Driving is on the left-hand side of the road. Main roads are generally safe but may have potholes, and secondary rural roads can be narrow and rough. Public transport is available, with a one-way ticket typically costing around £1 and a monthly pass £10.
*   **Culture & Social Life:** Be prepared for a slower pace of life ('island time'). Politeness, good manners, and respect are highly valued. Engaging with the local community, supporting local businesses, and participating in cultural events can aid integration.
*   **Prohibited Items/Activities:** Wearing any form of camouflage is illegal in Barbados. Possession and distribution of illegal drugs are strictly prohibited and carry severe penalties.
*   **Work Culture:** The work culture is generally formal, hierarchical, and relationship-oriented. Punctuality and professional appearance are important.
